data.name: Amoli
data.gender_notes: Amoli is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Amoli is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Amrita' which means nectar. In Hindu mythology, the gods churned the ocean to obtain the elixir of life, Amrita. This name is a reminder of the divine blessings and abundance in life. The name Amoli carries the meaning “Nectar of the gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amoli usually hope their child will grow to embody nectar of the gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Amoli belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Nectar of the gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amoli total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Amoli, also known as Amba, was a prominent Jain queen and a disciple of Mahavira. She belonged to the Lichchhavi clan and ruled in the 6th century BCE over what is now known as the Tarai region in Nepal and parts of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
Amoliputra, another name for the Hindu king Sasanka, ruled over Gauda (Bengal) during the 7th century CE. He is known for his patronage of Buddhism and temples, particularly of the goddess Tara.

modern_usage.modern_context: Amoli is a traditional Hindu name that has gained popularity in modern contexts. It is often used in Indian and Hindu communities as a unique and meaningful name for girls. The name Amoli is seen on various platforms including social media, where it appears in the form of hashtags and handles, baby name websites, where it is listed among trending and unique baby names, and YouTube, where it is featured in videos related to Indian culture and name meanings. General trends show an increasing interest in preserving cultural heritage by naming children with traditional names, while also giving them a modern and unique touch. Amoli is a perfect example of this trend, as it maintains its cultural significance while also being a distinct and beautiful name.
